header_summary:
A comprehensive draft standard for transaction inclusion proofs using wtxid has been proposed, consolidating divergent formats from Knots, Electrum, and other projects to define explicit validation requirements and interoperability guidelines. The draft, available at [this GitHub link](https://github.com/jeanpablojp/bips/blob/witness-inclusion-proofs/bip-witness-inclusion-proofs.md), introduces two proof formats, robust test vectors, and recommendations to mitigate Merkle branch vulnerabilities, particularly for lightweight clients, as detailed in the [mailing list discussion](https://gnusha.org/pi/bitcoindev/C899B11E-4971-4AAF-8BA3-81EBAFBF7739@jeanpablo.jp/T/#u#meb2b2f0670b30c170d2e4099b87537be5c558448).

Bitcoin Core versions 31.3 and 30.5 have been released to address a medium severity security vulnerability, with the fix already present in version 32.1. Full details and upgrade instructions are provided in the [security advisory](https://bitcoincore.org/en/2026/11/20/disclose-orphan-inv-stall/) and [release notes](https://bitcoincore.org/en/2026/11/20/release-30.5/), and users of older versions are strongly advised to update promptly for continued reliability ([mailing list thread](https://gnusha.org/pi/bitcoindev/c47ceea6-99de-41fe-a97c-928881963eccn@googlegroups.com/T/u)).

Recent technical discussions emphasize the importance of avoiding arbitrary limitations in TapScript, advocating for flexible mechanisms like the varops budget and isolated signature stacks to support advanced scripting and future upgrades ([relevant discussion](https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/segwit-commitment-to-post-quantum-witness-data/2702)). Additionally, transaction security can be enhanced by adopting opt-in rebroadcasting features, as outlined in [pull requests 36398](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36398) and [36481](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36481), to mitigate adversarial exploitation of wallet transaction propagation ([discussion](https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/exploiting-wallet-rebroadcast-to-link-addresses-to-node-ips-and-more/3123/4)).

The Segwit2x mailing list archive, reconstructed from the Wayback Machine, is now available at [learnbitcoin.com](https://www.learnbitcoin.com/archive/lists/segwit2x), providing accurate threading and restored internal links. Further archival efforts are underway for the lightning-dev mailing list, with community contributions welcomed to ensure completeness ([mailing list announcement](https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/we-made-the-bitcoin-dev-mailing-list-readable-15-years-24-699-messages/2985/7)).

recent_posts.title: [BIP Proposal] Witness Transaction Inclusion Proofs
recent_posts.summary: - A draft standardizes transaction inclusion proofs using wtxid by consolidating various approaches and providing extensive test vectors.  - It introduces explicit segwit status input, addresses Merkle branch complexity, and proposes proof rejection rules for edge cases.  - Two proof formats are detailed, and feedback is requested to enhance interoperability across Bitcoin applications.

recent_posts.title: Bitcoin Core security advisory for an easily discoverable vulnerability
recent_posts.summary: - Two new software releases address a medium severity security vulnerability in all supported versions.  - Detailed information and security policies are available in the linked official advisory and advisories page.  - Users of version 29.x are advised to upgrade to ensure their systems' safety and reliability.

recent_posts.title: Bitcoin Core v30.5 Released
recent_posts.summary: - Bitcoin Core v30.5 delivers bug fixes, performance upgrades, and enhanced internationalization with broad OS compatibility.  - Upgrading requires shutting down existing clients, following OS-specific steps, and supports stable migration.  - Notable improvements include unique inventory processing, continuous integration updates, and wide community contributions.

recent_posts.title: Handling PQ signatures on the stack
recent_posts.summary: - Upgradable limits in TapScript prevent unnecessary restrictions and facilitate future protocol improvements without legacy issues.  - Blacklisting opcodes and selective optimization both hinder innovative script uses and may introduce vulnerabilities.  - Implementing a variable operations budget or using an isolated signature stack enables flexible, secure, and scalable scripting.

recent_posts.title: We made the bitcoin-dev mailing list readable: 15 years, 24,699 messages
recent_posts.summary: - The Segwit2x mailing list archive, now available online, contains 722 messages across 75 threads.  - Message threading and permalinks were preserved using monthly files and links to original Wayback snapshots.  - Internal links were fixed, unified people pages created, and contributor help is requested for archive verification.

recent_posts.title: Exploiting Wallet Rebroadcast to Link Addresses to Node IPs and More
recent_posts.summary: - Pull request 36482 only slightly increases attack costs and fails to prevent them effectively.  - Making rebroadcasting opt-in grants users explicit control over their wallet-related transactions' propagation.  - Maintaining inactive features when users do not opt in helps prevent unintended propagation and adversarial exploitation.

active_posts.title: Re: RFC: Two years of BIP Editing, time for some new faces?
active_posts.summary: - Significant advancements include a new BIP process, updated documents, and enhanced repository integration scripts.  - Increasing editor workload highlighted the need for a refreshed, consistently active team of three editors.  - Continued collaboration and editorial renewal are proposed to sustain momentum and manage responsibilities effectively.

active_posts.title: SHRINCS: an efficient hash-based signature scheme for Bitcoin (first draft)
active_posts.summary: - The SHRINCS proposal introduces a semi-stateful hash-based signature scheme providing compact, post-quantum security.  - Limitations include state counter management, computational demands, and lack of test vectors or security proofs.  - Community feedback is encouraged to enhance SHRINCS' design, parameters, and cryptographic clarity.

active_posts.title: Quantum Landmines and Vulnerable Coin Auctions
active_posts.summary: - Quantum Landmine and auction mechanisms penalize attackers and enhance security for legacy cryptocurrency outputs.  - Staked and Sats Auctions use game theory and incentives to deter quantum-based theft of vulnerable coins.  - Design flexibility and adaptive strategies are crucial, as optimal solutions vary and threats evolve over time.

active_posts.title: Bounds on chain length with BIP-54 timewarp fixes
active_posts.summary: - Timewarp attack rules in Bitcoin restrict block timestamps to prevent manipulative behaviors and attacks.  - Mathematical modeling provides an upper bound formula for blockchain length under these security constraints.  - A formal proof confirms the effectiveness and correctness of these protections, ensuring blockchain reliability.

active_posts.title: SHRINCS: 324-byte stateful post-quantum signatures with static backups
active_posts.summary: - SHRINCS is a hybrid signature scheme combining efficient stateful and robust stateless cryptographic operations.  - It uses an unbalanced XMSS tree for efficient stateful signatures and defaults to stateless when needed.  - A fail-safe mechanism allows secure operation even if state management is compromised or uncertain.

active_posts.title: Reducing Bitcoin Full Node Storage Without Consensus Changes
active_posts.summary: - BitcoinRocks v31.1.1 introduces RocksDB, Zstandard compression, and parallelized block processing for improved efficiency.  - It maintains Bitcoin’s consensus rules and allows users to select local relay-policy profiles for flexibility.  - Extensive validation confirms complete chain agreement, and initial storage tests show significant space savings.

today_in_history_posts.title: A DNS-like decentralized mapping for wallet addresses?
today_in_history_posts.summary: - Mandar Mulherkar proposed a decentralized, user-friendly mapping service for converting crypto addresses.  - A responder recommended exploring Blockstack, which is developing a similar solution.  - Users were cautioned against sending sensitive information they would not share with the NSA.

today_in_history_posts.title: Directionality of the transaction fees
today_in_history_posts.summary: - The writer requests information about configuring channels to set direction-dependent transaction fees.  - Adjusting fees based on balance may help prevent channel imbalance and reduce associated risks.  - Automating these fee adjustments in Lightning Network applications would be an ideal solution.

today_in_history_posts.title: Disclosure: Critical vulnerabilities fixed in LND 0.19.0
today_in_history_posts.summary: - LND version 0.19.0 fixes critical vulnerabilities, including denial of service and theft risks.  - The update addresses attacks exploiting memory resources, failback vulnerabilities, and delays in HTLC claims.  - Users should promptly upgrade to protect their funds from these significant security threats.
